# HappyToHelp target product contract

Target edition · 17 October 2026 · US-first, USD. HappyToHelp is a complete customer service help desk and AI support agent for a US SMB support lead switching from Zendesk, Intercom (with Fin), Help Scout or Freshdesk. It owns the job from customer intake through a shared operational queue, self-service and live business context to an authorized resolution and continued customer recovery. Decagon, Sierra and Pylon set the agent/procedure and B2B-channel baseline; the target goes further with verified repair and obligations that survive handoffs.

## Product target

HappyToHelp is the complete help desk and AI support agent a US SMB support lead buys instead of Zendesk, Intercom (with Fin), Help Scout or Freshdesk; Decagon, Sierra and Pylon set the agent and procedure baseline it must also meet.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Category | Customer service help desks and AI support agents |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | Zendesk, Intercom (with Fin), Help Scout, Freshdesk (agent baseline: Decagon, Sierra, Pylon) |
| Up-and-comers it must also beat | Decagon, Sierra, Pylon |
| First buyer | A US SMB support lead, costs in USD, moving a Zendesk, Intercom, Help Scout or Freshdesk help desk |

The primary journey: Set up the workspace, bring in support history, connect customer channels, triage and assign requests, resolve them with knowledge and permitted actions, then verify recovery and follow up.

## How to read this contract

- This follows the RER contract standard.
- Core, Agent surface and Later are reported separately.
- Done means every acceptance outcome has recorded proof.
- Field proof records real-world qualification separately.
- ACCEPTANCE.md, docs/CLAIMS.md and summary counts are generated from this file.

## Door rules

- **D-1.** Support identity. Linking customers supplies staff context only; it grants no customer-side access, merge or send authority. Each customer continues to use their own verified session.
- **D-2.** Support recovery. A provider acknowledgment, closed engineering issue or completed command is not customer recovery; record the separate observation.

### Retained product and operating guarantees

#### NATIVE-001 — Native owner installation

**Requirement.** The owner can inspect the operating description before dependency installation; setup preserves this edition’s native owner and selected bindings. Local setup exits with no app running; dev prints a private entry address that enters as the real local owner through the rer dev v2 boundary, preserving native sessions, roles and passwords. Reset is explicitly confirmed and local; export/import preserve supported native data with documented exclusions. Deployment dry-run makes zero outbound requests and explicitly reports that fact. A separately and explicitly started read-only provider preflight uses the owner's scoped Cloudflare token with owner consent to read the account's Workers subdomain and the Worker's settings and secret names (three GETs for an existing Worker); it sends no mail and changes no resources. Dry-run and preflight are independent steps, neither a mock of the other. The delivered runtime requires no original checkout or PHP service. Details are in [the support protocol guide](docs/contract/support-protocols.md).

**Acceptance.**
1. Use a clean checkout through rer describe/check, locked installation, setup, dev, verify, reset and export/import; preserve owner/data/settings and refuse unconfirmed destructive work.
2. For deployment dry-run, assert zero outbound requests and an explicit no-outbound report without provider credentials.
3. As a separate acceptance point, explicitly start the read-only provider preflight with owner consent and the owner's scoped token; assert only the three expected Cloudflare GETs for an existing Worker, no mail and no mutations, and refuse missing credentials or consent.
4. Prove the runtime works independently of the original checkout; separately qualify remote provisioning.

#### IDENTITY-002 — Retained native password identity

**Requirement.** Preserve native password sign-in, first-owner setup, the accepted owner experience and prior account/workspace data with the maintained Base command mechanisms. Retain this edition's authentication and native owner setup. A second factor for these native accounts is required by IDENTITY-003; it adds to native passwords and never replaces them. Supersedes `BASE-ACCESS-001` for native password identity under RL-1.

**Acceptance.**
1. Complete native password setup, login, recovery and workspace re-entry, then upgrade with prior owner credentials and data intact; configured providers must not replace native identity.

#### IDENTITY-001 — Scoped authority

**Requirement.** Owner setup, registration, login/recovery, project switching, membership and widget admission establish native identity. Provider configuration never substitutes for user authority. The public widget key and origin are not a secret: visitor, registration and project-creation requests are bounded by D1-backed limits (the documented admission limits) and refused with HTTP 429 and `Retry-After`. A stored widget session serves only the visitor identity the host page supplies now (its identifier, else its email in any letter case, else anonymous); an unsigned sign-in carries the browser's anonymous conversation over, unverified; and `h2h('shutdown')` ends the browser's widget sessions.

**Acceptance.**
1. Through native session and widget routes, deny cross-tenant, blocked/deleted and revoked access; prove public admission returns 429 with Retry-After when limited and provider configuration conveys no actor authority.
2. In one real browser against the emitted Worker and the built widget, prove that account switches, sign-out, emulated pages and signed identities never send, read or render another visitor's session or conversation; that sign-in carries the anonymous conversation over and a returning signed-in visitor gets its own back; and that `h2h('shutdown')` removes the widget and forgets the browser's sessions in every state.

#### FIRST-RUN-001 — A useful first workspace

**Requirement.** First-run setup is one screen: the owner's email, a password, the website and, only where the server requires one, the private setup token. Missing names and colors are derived and every derived value can be changed. A completed installation leads the owner to a workspace that is already set up, whose Setup page lists only what cannot be done for them (an AI service key, the widget on their website and, with a hosted email provider, a verified sending domain), leads with the widget, lets the owner skip any of them for now, and shows everything else under "What we've set". Every workspace created by first-owner setup, signed-in workspace creation or email-verified registration, and never a demo workspace, is provisioned in one step: a starter assistant as its default visitor assistant, a reply-by-email mailbox when the installation holds the installation’s inbound-email credential, and mail sent from the installation sender until the workspace's own domain is verified. The starter assistant’s visitor replies carry external, and its internal preparation standard; the company’s policy decides each call once a provider key and complete policy exist, within that policy’s AI spending limits; with no key no assistant is assigned to a new conversation, it stays with the team and the AI page and Setup say a key is missing. The first-run Create workspace action may send one welcome email to the owner; an uncertain send is never replayed. Ordinary workspace creation leads with the widget snippet; Advanced retains the server secret and verification examples. Empty inboxes offer installation, a link to Setup and a demo. Workspace headers follow workspace switching. Visitor headers retain the operator's display name.

**Acceptance.**
1. Run fresh first-owner setup and signed-in workspace creation to Setup and an installable widget; inspect derived editable name/color, starter assistant, mailbox/sender, skip/Advanced controls and mobile headers.
2. With no model key a new visitor stays with the team; with a configured provider exercise the capped starter.
3. A workers.dev hostname must not become a business name.

#### LOCAL-MAIL-001 — Rer dev mail

**Requirement.** Trusted local development configuration uses the rer dev v2 development transport: it validates and suppresses visitor and teammate mail, reports `development`, stores no messages and exposes no mail viewer. It sends no external email. The local owner enters automatically through the dev boundary; native password identity, ordinary hosted email-link confirmation and prior stored data are retained. Production has no local dev surface. Missing credentials or failed remote delivery never select a local substitute.

**Acceptance.**
1. Enter through rer dev v2; send visitor and teammate mail and prove development suppression without storage, viewer or external send; refuse forged and production dev entry and never substitute suppression for a failed hosted provider.

#### CONVERSATION-001 — Durable transcript

**Requirement.** Customer, operator, generation, import and administrative writers preserve stable message/command identity, revision/frontier, attachment ownership and final-reply admission atomically. Competing or repeated writes cannot admit two incompatible final replies. Owner/admin contact erasure removes message content while keeping identity, revision and frontier, so erased transcripts stay coherent.

**Acceptance.**
1. Race visitor, operator, model and import writers through conversation routes with duplicate and lost responses; admit only compatible final replies.
2. Erase a contact through the owner door and verify coherent identity/revision/frontier with content removed.

#### DELIVERY-001 — Live delivery and recovery

**Requirement.** Persist before broadcast; reconnect/outbox replay and socket authorization recover committed messages after reload, disconnection or process wake. Provisional AI deltas never become durable final answers until guarded admission succeeds.

**Acceptance.**
1. Disconnect/reconnect widget and operator sockets after persisted writes, restart the runtime and recover the same committed messages/attachments; unauthorized replay is denied and superseded AI deltas never become final replies.

#### UI-001 — Existing editable experience

**Requirement.** Reuse the original React dashboard, transcripts/drafts/suggestions, settings and Shadow DOM widget; preserve useful desktop/mobile flows, attachment display, collector/privacy controls and errors. Native routing and transport use the configured application origin.

**Acceptance.**
1. Use the native dashboard and separately installed widget at 1440 and 390 pixels with realistic conversations, attachments, drafts, errors and workspace switching; retain the approved desktop/mobile navigation and configured-origin transport.

#### MOVE-IN-001 — Reviewed history import

**Requirement.** Current workspace owner/admin reviewers privately upload, inspect per-kind plans, source-located omissions, rejections, conflicts and publication changes, then explicitly apply bounded, resumable imports of conversations, contacts, tags, saved replies and articles. Preserve source identities, timestamps, private notes and publication state; reject unsupported meaning rather than inventing it. Recheck current role and workspace authority for apply, resume and whole-import undo. Retain immutable source custody and conflict-safe reversal journals. Imports and undo send no mail, widget messages, model requests, assignment or connection notifications; imports are excluded from Reports. Native tag controls enforce workspace scope. RL-2 requires exact business-state repeat/undo equality, including contacts, conversations, messages, private notes, tags, source links and every other imported business table. Only platform counters/sequences, audit history and import journals are excluded. Synthetic 1,000-conversation datasets for Zendesk and Help Scout qualify this local flow.

**Acceptance.**
1. Through Move in, exercise all five kinds, source custody, per-row omissions/rejections/conflicts, current-role denials, inert apply/resume/repeat/undo and exact business-state equality for synthetic 1,000-conversation Zendesk and Help Scout datasets; counters/sequences, audit and journals are the only named exclusions.

#### OUTCOMES-001 — Resolution feedback and provenance

**Requirement.** Current original visitor sessions may rate a closed resolution with thumbs up/down and an optional comment up to 1,000 characters. Changes retain history; reopened cycles cannot receive the previous resolution's rating. Operators retain access to each past resolution's latest feedback after reopening; visitor eligibility and report denominators remain tied to the current cycle. Erasure removes rating comments. Confirmed operator-sent drafts establish assisted outcomes, otherwise confirmed human replies establish human outcomes. AI requires a complete visible answer history without a person handoff; missing evidence remains unknown. Status, assignment and cancellation transitions recheck current authority atomically.

**Acceptance.**
1. Close, rate, rerate, reopen and close again via widget/operator routes; prevent previous-session/cycle feedback, retain old-cycle operator visibility, redact erased comments and verify human/assisted/AI/unknown attribution from actual visible answers.

#### REPORTS-001 — Workspace calendar reports

**Requirement.** Native conversations created in the workspace IANA calendar range with at least one persisted message form the cohort; Move in and legacy imports are excluded. First visitor-to-visible-answer response and creation-to-first known-resolution durations use median and nearest-rank p90. Each conversation contributes its latest closed cycle once to outcome and satisfaction rates. Reopened conversations leave those denominators. Aggregate queries return bounded data; CSV streams every matching conversation with formula-safe cells. Empty widget conversations stay durable but are excluded from Reports and its analytics CSVs. A separate step-up guarded JSON export includes all workspace conversations, messages, private notes and attachment names across dates and imports; attachment bytes stay in the portable backup.

**Acceptance.**
1. Compare Reports and formula-safe CSV to hand-calculated response/resolution median and p90, latest-cycle outcome and satisfaction cohorts across DST and tenants, including more than 10,000 rows and excluded imports/reopened cycles.

#### CONNECTIONS-001 — Workspace integrations

**Requirement.** Owner/admin tokens have explicit scopes, optional expiry, one-time display, hashed storage and durable audit. Bearer-only API calls have no CORS, per-token limits and native guarded writes. Contact erasure fences API identity restoration and pending event payloads. Native events commit tenant-bound webhook and Slack intents; historical import apply and undo do not emit them. Slack projects bounded native visitor text through Base escaping. The owner-authorized ordinary HTTPS exception retains redirect refusal, bounded requests/responses and literal-destination checks instead of DNS pinning (RL-3). See [the full transport exception](docs/contract/support-protocols.md).

**Acceptance.**
1. Issue, use, expire and revoke each scoped show-once token; exercise native API operations, erasure fences, signed events and Slack escaping.
2. Refuse redirects/unsafe literal destinations and over-limit traffic; preserve timeout, streamed bounds, uncertain 500 without replay and bounded 429 behavior under the recorded HTTPS override.

#### ACTIVATION-001 — Observed owner setup

**Requirement.** An owner sees the durable, project-scoped eight-step list on the Setup page; the genuinely empty inbox shows one next action and a link to it, and loads none of it. A step is confirmed only by an observation, never by a saved configuration, an installer default or a preset, so a workspace with nothing observed yet is zero of its applicable steps. The system runs its own checks: while an owner is signed in the page asks the server to observe, bounded by freshness windows. These checks are non-generative metadata, domain and DNS reads and never send mail. They distinguish saved configuration from observed sender DNS, authenticated model metadata, an inbound receipt, effective runtime ceilings, allowed origin and an authenticated widget ping; whether an article is published is not one of them (that step stays among the eight ids but is hidden and never counted). Mail to the owner is confirmed by a used emailed sign-in link, or by the provider's reported outcome for the welcome or test email; local development mail is suppressed and never confirms delivery, and provider acceptance or queueing is pending. Reading Setup performs no provider work and writes nothing. Only an explicit owner action (Create workspace, or Send me a test) may send mail, to that owner's mailbox, with durable identity; ambiguous work is never replayed. Missing provider permissions and unsupported status APIs remain unavailable. Configuration changes invalidate observations; model and DNS validation expire after 15 minutes and every observation shows its time. The owner can skip an owner-only step (the widget, the AI service, the sending domain) for now, and undo it. A skip is stored on the server for the workspace, can be made by an owner or admin only, makes no provider request, and moves the step out of Needs you and out of the confirmed count and its total; a skipped step is never shown as confirmed. An observation always wins: a skipped step that is later observed is confirmed and counted, and a rejected provider key stays under Needs you whether or not it was skipped. Provider keys and their fingerprints never enter API responses or browser storage. Details are in [the support protocol guide](docs/contract/support-protocols.md).

**Acceptance.**
1. Read Setup without side effects, observe fresh/expired/rejected configuration and explicit provider outcomes, skip/undo owner steps and reload.
2. A skip or preset never counts as confirmation; local suppression never proves delivery; keys/fingerprints remain server-only and uncertain explicit test/welcome mail is never replayed.

#### AI-001 — Configured model execution

**Requirement.** Retain Ensemble model selection, context/tools, streamed events, normalization, raw per-round provider usage, attribution, bounded suggestions and reply lifecycle. Missing providers fail explicitly when AI is asked for, and a default assistant whose provider has no key is simply not assigned to new conversations; uncertain provider attempts remain uncertain and are not replayed automatically. Usage is diagnostic/provider accounting data, not an active payment, balance or debit system. Visitor-caused model work carries the classes of its eventual action, and the company’s policy sets its project and installation AI spending limits; a skipped reply is recorded as terminal and never replayed. Each workspace's AI reply mode is auto (the default), draft or off: in draft AI writes only drafts its team sends themselves, in off AI generates nothing, no AI-authored message reaches a customer in draft or off by any path (a local computer agent's reply becomes a draft its operator sends themselves, and a visitor whose assistant will not answer is handled as one without an assistant), in draft or off a conversation whose visitor has written since its assistant last answered is listed in the team's normal views as one without an assistant, and switching back to auto releases nothing queued, written or due during that time.

**Acceptance.**
1. Request configured suggestions/replies through native routes; inspect normalized streaming events, per-round usage, context/tool and budget bounds, explicit missing-provider errors and durable daily-cap skips; crash/ambiguous attempts must not automatically replay.

#### KNOWLEDGE-001 — Published knowledge

**Requirement.** Dataset ingestion/crawl, retained corpus, lexical/selected semantic retrieval, citations and article/category authoring maintain project scope and publication state. A failed refresh cannot replace the last usable published corpus. Public pages exclude drafts/deleted projects and preserve original canonical article/search routes.

**Acceptance.**
1. Publish and search articles/categories through authoring and public help-center doors; deny draft/deleted/cross-project access, verify citations and canonical links and retain the last usable published corpus after a failed refresh.

#### CONTEXT-001 — Attributed customer context

**Requirement.** Profiles, monitoring, insights and context packets preserve evidence attribution, source bounds, consent and project ownership. Provider output must satisfy the selected schemas before becoming usable customer context.

**Acceptance.**
1. Generate/read profile, monitoring, insight and context packets through native routes; reject ungrounded/schema-invalid or cross-project content, preserve attributed evidence and respect consent/source bounds.

#### DELEGATION-001 — Explicit local authority

**Requirement.** Pairing, devices/grants, revocation, tool context and work/result states preserve investigation, resolve and advance-authorized resolve-and-reply distinctions. Revocation withdraws authority and never asserts that a local process stopped: started work becomes terminal with an unconfirmed outcome, and only the device may report cancellation. Local processes remain in the optional connector, never an implicit Worker capability. Agent calls use the company’s policy for their computed classes; any approval or review in this journey is under the held company policy.

**Acceptance.**
1. Under the held company policy, pair the packaged connector, investigate, separately authorize a child fix, obtain a distinct read-only observation and use human Send with exact-request replay.
2. Under the held company policy, refuse stale/revoked/offline/unverified/uncertain work and distinguish resolve from advance-authorized resolve-and-reply; revocation cannot assert process cancellation.

#### TRAINING-001 — Durable evaluation

**Requirement.** Training and evaluation preserve run/case state, model/budget selection, raw provider usage and cancellation/recovery. Synthetic data admission is explicitly local/test-only. Historical pending attempts require reconciliation; a fixture pass is not live-provider quality acceptance.

**Acceptance.**
1. Create, run, cancel and recover persisted evaluations through training routes with model/budget selection and raw usage; reconcile historical pending/uncertain attempts and keep synthetic admission local/test-only.

#### INTEGRATION-001 — Honest external effects

**Requirement.** Email/inbound mail, GitHub, branding and knowledge imports use configured native adapters, tenant-scoped credentials, durable identity and ambiguous-outcome handling. Website previews use a separate origin, scoped expiring grants and public-network restrictions. ## Target clauses

### Complete support operations

#### DESK-001 — The shared support desk

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ROLE-001, BASE-INPUT-003

**Requirement.** A visitor starts website live chat, identifies themselves under the workspace policy, sends files and returns to their history. Humans see one durable shared inbox with customer history, scoped retained-history search with words, quoted phrases and literal customer-identity matching, open/closed/mine/unassigned/AI/tag filters and saved replies that insert into the composer without silently sending. Ticket status follows the STATUS-001 lifecycle and saved replies extend to MACRO-001 action macros. Replies, attachment downloads and errors are visible on both sides; privacy/collector controls remain effective.

**Acceptance.**
1. Through the installed widget and operator inbox, exchange messages and real attachment bytes, search/filter the resulting queue, insert and edit a saved reply, reload both sides and deny another tenant the same records.

#### WIDGET-001 — Availability-aware messenger and proactive messages

*Tier:* Core

**Requirement.** The messenger shows team availability from business-hour schedules (SLA-001) and live agent presence. When no human or permitted AI assistant is available it says so with the expected reply time, captures the visitor's email (or, where consented, SMS/WhatsApp under CHANNELS-001) so the answer reaches them, and creates the ticket instead of leaving the visitor waiting. Leads configure proactive messages triggered by page URL, time on page, scroll depth, exit intent, visitor attributes, returning visit or cart value, with audience, brand, frequency caps and quiet hours. Each proactive message shows a clear sender identity and an easy dismiss, respects consent and collector settings, and never starts a conversation that sends personal data on the visitor's behalf. Impressions, opens, dismissals and resulting conversations and resolutions are reported. This clause backs the homepage hero's "Before they ask".

**Acceptance.**
1. Outside configured hours, open the installed widget, see the offline message and expected reply time, leave an email and verify the ticket and the emailed answer.
2. During hours with no agent online verify the same; with an available AI assistant verify it answers and discloses itself.
3. Configure a proactive message on a checkout URL after 20 seconds with a once-per-day cap; verify it appears once, dismisses, stays silent under a declined collector setting and appears in reports with its impressions and conversations.

#### MAIL-001 — Complete support email

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-MAIL-001, BASE-OPS-003 · *Register:* R-2

**Requirement.** Connect inbound forwarding, an IMAP/SMTP mailbox, Gmail/Google Workspace or Microsoft 365/Outlook using scoped credentials/OAuth. New mail creates tickets and replies thread by stable Message-ID/In-Reply-To/References with deliberate handling of changed subject, aliases and multiple recipients. Operators manage CC/BCC, attachments, signatures and branded sender/reply addresses. Duplicate/redelivered mail, bounces, spam and auto-responders cannot create loops or send twice, and mail classified as spam or failing sender checks goes to the reviewable Suspended view of MAIL-002; reconnect/backfill has a visible cursor and errors, and removal stops new intake without deleting history.

**Acceptance.**
1. For each of forwarding, IMAP, Gmail and Microsoft 365, use the connection UI and provider sandboxes or official-schema fakes to receive a new thread, reply from the inbox, receive its follow-up and attachment, disconnect/reconnect with redelivery and observe bounce/permission failure.
2. Verify no duplicate ticket/reply or machine-mail AI loop; keep provider-protocol tests separate from live acceptance.
3. Spam and failing-sender mail reaches the MAIL-002 Suspended view, not a ticket.

#### MAIL-002 — Reviewable suspended and spam mail

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-MAIL-001, BASE-DATA-002, BASE-ROLE-001, BASE-AUDIT-001

**Requirement.** Inbound mail that is spam-scored, fails DMARC/SPF/DKIM or alignment, comes from a blocked sender or domain, forges a verified customer's address, exceeds size limits or is a detected mail loop is never silently dropped. It lands in a Suspended view with its reason, authentication results, headers and safely previewed attachments, and creates no ticket, AI work, acknowledgment or notification. Permitted operators recover a false positive into a normal ticket that threads correctly (into the existing ticket when its references match) without retroactively triggering acknowledgments or AI unless they choose to; delete true spam; and block or allow a sender or domain. Recovery, deletion and list changes are audited. Suspended mail is kept for a stated retention period (default 14 days) and then explicitly deleted with an audit record; the view shows counts and the oldest age so nothing ages out unseen. Allow/block lists and suspension reasons are reportable.

**Acceptance.**
1. Through the application’s inbound doors deliver a spam-scored message, a DMARC-failing message, mail from a blocked sender and a forged From of a known customer; verify each appears in Suspended with its reason and creates no ticket, AI request or outbound mail.
2. Recover the DMARC-failing message into a new ticket and another into its existing thread, delete the spam, allow-list a sender and redeliver.
3. Advance the clock past retention at the runtime edge and verify explicit, audited deletion; refuse every action to a role without permission.

#### STATUS-001 — Ticket status lifecycle

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ROLE-001

**Requirement.** Every ticket has one status from a lifecycle the lead can extend: New, Open, Pending (waiting on the customer), On-hold (waiting on an internal team or third party), Solved and Closed, plus workspace custom statuses that each map to one of those categories. A customer reply to a Pending or On-hold ticket returns it to Open and wakes its owner. On-hold and every internal status label are never shown to the customer, who sees an open request in the widget, portal and email. A customer reply to a Solved ticket reopens it. After a lead-configured period (default 4 days) a durable time-based automation (AUTOMATION-002) moves Solved to Closed, and Closed is final: a customer reply to a Closed ticket creates a new follow-up ticket linked to it that carries the requester, CCs, tags and fields. Status filters, sorts, views, bulk edits (QUEUE-002), SLA pausing (SLA-001), resolution cycles (OUTCOMES-001) and reports all use this lifecycle, and every change records its actor, time and source (person, rule, automation or customer reply).

**Acceptance.**

Assign the ticket, add a follower, update it as the customer and mention a teammate; verify each notification reaches only permitted current members according to preference, a revoked member receives nothing, a group notification reaches the group and an uncertain provider send stays uncertain without a second send.

#### ZENDESK-IMPORT-001 — Offline Zendesk tickets and conversation history

*Tier:* Core · *From:* new · *Cites:* BASE-ROLE-001, BASE-OPS-003, BASE-DATA-001, BASE-DATA-003 · *Rules:* D-1

**Requirement.** A current workspace owner or admin imports wholly synthetic offline Zendesk exports through the existing mounted Move in upload, review and apply flow and its native target adapter. It is an export reader, not a Zendesk service adapter: no provider calls, credentials, real customer exports or live cutover are inputs. It preserves MOVE-IN-001 inertness and exact business-state repeat/undo, MIGRATION-001 erasure precedence, MOVE-IN-003 threading and the existing Freshdesk attachment limits, media guards and bytes. Historical metrics never install or activate SLA policies.

**Acceptance.** Through Move in, native ticket and media reads and native erasure, with a synthetic offline corpus:
1. A realistic corpus with Zendesk-shaped field names and explicit source relationships enters through the mounted upload/review door, including split or out-of-order users, organizations and tickets, repeated IDs, an unknown field, a missing comment page and an export that declares incomplete comments. Wrapped JSONL/NDJSON stays supported; each additional accepted layout, and how separately supplied comment, audit and metric files join ticket IDs, is documented. An optional packer reads local files only and keeps record provenance; it is neither a network exporter nor an alternate importer. Incomplete conversations and unsupported meaning are refused or visibly reported with file, row, pointer and source ID, never silently truncated, and retained-but-unmapped records never count as native successes. Fixtures use example-domain addresses and `synthetic-hh-<n>` identifiers (numeric source IDs where Zendesk requires them) within the documented upload and record limits; supported splitting is documented instead of raising the limits.
2. Preview and applied native tickets reconcile exact counts and IDs for requesters, organizations, public comments versus internal notes, tags, supported typed fields and status categories. Author roles and source timestamps survive without creating logins, verified customer sessions, domain-derived entitlement, active assignment or company-wide access; ownership review and threading keep their current behavior. New, Open, Pending, Hold, Solved and Closed stay distinct, Closed keeps its native follow-up behavior, and unsupported custom statuses and field meanings are listed in the report. A reloaded ticket keeps its source provenance and typed values, and private notes never reach a visitor or another workspace.
3. Supplied attachment bytes import and download byte-exactly through native media access. Actual Zendesk `id`, `file_name`, `content_type`, `size` and `content_url` metadata is supported, and separately supplied local bytes bind through a documented, unambiguous attachment-ID/path binding with digest and size checks. An untouched export never needs an undocumented `base64` field, and any local packing representation is clearly distinguished from the source format. No URL is fetched: a URL-only attachment shows visibly as missing bytes, never as a successful binary import. Mismatched bytes and ambiguous ownership are refused before any native effect. Public-comment and private-note attachments keep their visibility, duplicate file names keep distinct identities, and no other customer or workspace can download them. Credential-bearing URL parts are redacted before custody under the supported credential policy, and no signed access URL becomes portable data or a browser link.
4. Supplied source status transitions and SLA metric and audit history appear as inspectable, inert imported history in the existing imported-ticket and review views under current ticket authority, linked to source ticket and event IDs with timestamps, target or metric meaning and available elapsed units. Unknown and absent history stay distinguishable, including a missing events file and an unsupported event type. Nothing starts a native SLA clock, emits a breach alert, changes an active policy, charges usage or synthesizes source compliance, and no procedure, reporting or MOVE-IN-004 policy activation work rides along. The history is part of the adapter's fingerprints, repeat/undo equality, erasure and portable custody, never an untracked JSON side store.
5. Review writes no native business state, and only a current owner or admin applies the exact reviewed fingerprint. An import stopped after a committed batch resumes after the reviewer reopens it and signs in again. Replaying the same export adds no business rows or objects; a corrected later export shows explicit changes and conflicts and keeps native edits; whole-import undo restores the exact prior business state while respecting native-edit conflicts. These counts include attachment objects and history stores as well as rows. Imports and undo make no provider or AI request, send no customer message, acknowledgment or assignment notification and do not inflate historical reports. Cross-workspace and revoked-reviewer attempts are refused through public doors, and the synthetic 1,000-conversation Zendesk capacity run carries realistic mixed statuses and history within current limits.
6. Erasing an imported requester through native erasure removes their comments, private notes, attachment bytes, organization-linked personal values and personal history from native reads and from retained original, plan, journal and portable copies, as current erasure semantics require. Tombstones and digests stop resume, same-file replay and a corrected re-upload from restoring them, for a retained import and for a new application attempt with the same source identity. Existing erasure and restore behavior holds, restore revives no revoked authority, and nothing calls the old production app.

An owner can require two-factor sign-in for every teammate or by role; affected users must enroll at their next sign-in before reaching any data, and existing sessions without the factor end.  Owner-assisted reset of a teammate's factor requires the owner's own recent factor, notifies the teammate and is audited; an owner who loses every factor recovers through the documented installation-level owner recovery through `rer`, never by email alone. Refund and billing approval (COMMERCE-001, BILLING-001), integration and credential installation, exports, erasure, role changes and the two-factor policy itself require a recent second-factor step-up. API access uses scoped tokens (CONNECTIONS-001), never a password alone. SSO users follow their identity provider's MFA (ACCESS-001). This adds to the retained native password identity (IDENTITY-002) and never replaces it.

**Acceptance.**
1. As owner require two-factor sign-in; sign in as a support operator and be forced to enroll TOTP and receive recovery codes; sign out and verify refusal without the factor, with a wrong code, with a reused code and with a used recovery code; sign in with a passkey.

### Agent surface

**Specialist: support agent.** It triages and resolves support requests, finds permitted knowledge and business context, carries out permitted repair and keeps customer recovery and follow-up attached to the original request.

Inherits BASE-AGENT-001 to BASE-AGENT-013. The company’s policy decides every call.

**How HappyToHelp computes each class.**
- **standard:** reversible internal drafts, ticket organization, triage, private knowledge edits and obligations; facts include affected item count.
- **external:** a reply, notification, share, published article or destination newly exposes support content outside the business; facts include recipients and known customer/vendor, new counterparty or public exposure. A proactive insight saved or generated for a visitor whose widget will show it is external, with recipient count and known, new or public counterparty facts.
- **money:** a Shopify refund, Stripe refund/subscription charge change or changed support-provider spending; facts include amount, currency and merchant/customer.
- **commitment:** a customer promise, accepted offer or editorial sign-off others rely on; facts include value and counterparty.
- **accounts:** connecting a service creates an outside provider account, number or paid resource; facts include provider and resource.
- **gated:** the provider reserves consent, hosted checkout, verification or personal terms to a person, including a provider response requiring that step; facts include provider and step.
- **access:** staff, selected knowledge, customer entitlements, devices or integration/agent grants change authority; facts include affected people and whether it widens or narrows.
- **security:** factor requirements, credentials, protected provider settings, recovery keys or protective transport configuration change; facts name the setting.
- **destructive:** erasure, permanent attachment deletion or replacement restore cannot be undone in the product; facts include item count.
- **sensitive:** a support request or connected record contains regulated identity, health, bank or payment data; facts include kind and record count.
- **live:** repair or a published routing, procedure or automation change affects a running service; facts identify that service.

## Boundaries

HappyToHelp owns customer support, its operational queue, service follow-up and support CSAT. It consumes sales/customer context from [Orbit](https://github.com/just-every/run-orbit), HubSpot and Salesforce; [Buoy](https://github.com/just-every/run-buoy) owns post-sale customer-success programs. [Penny](https://github.com/just-every/run-penny) owns feedback aggregation, prioritization, roadmap/changelog and requester closure; [Vector](https://github.com/just-every/run-vector) owns engineering issues and delivery. HappyToHelp links their records and follows the support request through verified recovery. General marketing campaigns go to [Mango](https://github.com/just-every/run-mango), incident subscriber communication to [Lamp](https://github.com/just-every/run-lamp), general survey research to [Pencil](https://github.com/just-every/run-pencil) and employee IT service management to [Linen](https://github.com/just-every/run-linen). No neighboring product or unowned LIST gap is absorbed.

Aircall/Twilio and Meta operate the telephone/messaging networks and provider registration; HappyToHelp supplies the connected support experience, routing, consent and failure controls in VOICE-001 and CHANNELS-001. It does not become a carrier or emergency dispatch service: emergency callers are directed to 911 through the provider's supported routing and disclosed number/location limitations, while US emergency-calling obligations for supplied numbers must be qualified before voice launch. Stripe/Shopify execute authorized financial actions; HappyToHelp neither holds funds nor stores raw payment credentials. Commerce, CRM and subscription ledgers remain in their respective systems; complete support actions remain required here.

Arbitrary repair execution runs only in an explicitly paired external workspace, with per-operation authority, never as an implicit Worker capability. Provider apps, native apps, production integration qualification, health-data agreements, consent rules and payments-related support actions are engineering obligations in the named clauses, not reasons to reduce the target. Regulated deployments require ASSURANCE-001 qualification; no current HIPAA, SOC 2 or FedRAMP assurance is claimed. Provider acceptance is not customer receipt, a passing fixture is not a live deployment and a completed tool call is not a verified customer outcome. Accessibility and the separate Base-data equivalence hold remain open; conversion supplies no qualification.

# HappyToHelp HappyToHelp is an open-source support workspace with a customer chat widget, shared inbox, AI-assisted replies, help centers, customer context and optional work delegated to your own Codex or Claude. It works with human replies without an AI provider. The editable React application runs on Cloudflare Workers with Hono, D1, R2, Queues and Durable Objects. ## Release 0.4.25 Deploy version 0.4.25, tagged **`v0.4.25`** once published. v0.4.24 is the upgrade baseline; upgrades are qualified from v0.4.24, v0.4.23 and v0.4.22. The pinned installer remains rer 0.2.112. - **Managed installation verification:** includes the generator-recorded portable contract anchor. A managed source copy with only its own two installation commits can now run the existing contract check without the publisher's Git history. Setup, build, verification and artifact creation keep their declared checks; this fixes the `contract_anchor_missing` failure after copying v0.4.24. - **Unused legacy reservations and attachment custody:** the original installation owner can approve a different package fingerprint after an unused adoption reservation expires, is discarded or pauses with an error, provided no destination workspace was created and no erasure or deletion fence applies. Created provenance remains permanent, and the old fingerprint stays closed. Canonical attachment custody transfers with the unused reservation, including already cleaned coordinates; old cleanup jobs cannot delete a replacement package's live attachments or stop its import wakeups. A cleanup already deleting objects must finish its claim before that handoff. - **Clearer imported history and results:** historical staff display as Former staff, while historical contact, AI and system authors retain their distinctions; none gains native membership or assignment authority. Move in shows the actual pause code and a matching explanation, distinguishes historical verification from current source availability, and labels historical memberships as granting no access. Reconciliation tables can be reached and scrolled with the keyboard, including on phones. Imported AI profiles remain disabled and imported workflows stay draft. - **Tickets and mailbox setup:** a ticket starting with an internal note can be created before a mailbox is connected, without sending email. Email-first tickets still require a connected mailbox. Email settings explain missing installation prerequisites and local-trial limits, with hosted Google, Microsoft, IMAP/SMTP and forwarding instructions. A local trial sends and receives no email; use website chat to try conversations. Connecting a mailbox does not configure sign-in or invitation mail. Live mailbox/provider qualification remains separate. - **Fresh hosted installs:** native setup, ordinary support and the ticket/mailbox guidance above are active. The importer runner and adoption remain inert until a legacy package is imported through the approved flow; cleanup continues for already registered packages. Updating alone starts no import, sends no mail and grants no historical-user access. The corrected mail declaration and rer 0.2.112 are retained. Real-customer remote importer use, signed migration-before-Worker delivery and live-provider qualification remain separate; this preparation authorizes no production import or cutover. - **Migrations:** no migrations since v0.4.24. The inventory remains 195 files, byte-identical to v0.4.24, so its applied migration ledger stays unchanged. A v0.4.23 installation applies 328, 329, 331 and 332 once in filename order BEFORE the new Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic; v0.4.22 first applies 327, retaining the published buyer steps. There is no migration 326 or 330. Update from v0.4.24 without resetting; v0.4.23 and v0.4.22 are also upgrade baselines. Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings first. Use Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and pinned rer 0.2.112. Retain native owners, permissions, support history, files, erasure fences and every applied migration identity. A v0.4.24 installation applies no migration. Stop the old Worker before applying any missing migrations on older installations: v0.4.23 applies 328_legacy_workspace_adoption.sql, 329_legacy_package_custody.sql, 331_legacy_cleanup_seeding.sql and 332_legacy_cleanup_inventory_lazy.sql once in that order BEFORE the new Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic; v0.4.22 first applies 327_legacy_import_worker.sql. Retain those releases' published buyer steps, including 332's conditional cleanup of only an untouched empty inventory marker. Earlier installations first apply every other missing published migration in filename order. There is no migration 326 or 330 in this release. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` against the retained installation before any separately authorized deployment. V1 source stays cleanup-only and must never be relabeled v2; incomplete cleanup remains pending. No reset, mail activation, recovery adoption, production import, cutover or production deployment is part of this preparation. See [RELEASE.json](RELEASE.json), [Updates and recovery](docs/INDEPENDENT-RELEASE.md) and [the changelog](CHANGELOG.md). Version 0.4.0 adds Move in for reviewed support-history imports, resolution feedback with workspace-calendar Reports, Connections with scoped API tokens, signed webhook events and Slack delivery, and the `rer` local path. Native passwords, owners and data are kept. Before the updated Worker serves traffic, back up and apply the ten additive migrations `0110_move_in.sql` to `119_local_portability.sql` in order; an existing 0.3 installation follows [Upgrading from 0.3.x](OPERATIONS.md#upgrading-from-03x). [The changelog](CHANGELOG.md) lists every change. Known limits: - Accessibility is on a confirmed owner **HOLD**; no WCAG conformance is claimed. - `rer export` archives cover D1, R2 and **Durable Object** storage (with a digest); full Base-data equivalence is not yet established. - Hosted operating costs are **unmeasured**; timed activation and paid-provider execution are not qualified. - Imports and connections are qualified with **synthetic fixtures** only, without real vendor exports or live Slack. - No hosted installation, compliance or FedRAMP qualification is claimed. - The hosted service at **app.happytohelp.com** is separate legacy production and is not part of this release. ## Run it on your computer The [install and run guide](docs/INSTALLER.md) covers installation, local sign-in and stopping the app, step by step. The [Run HappyToHelp page](https://happytohelp.com/run) has the quick-start command. Start it with one line. You need **Node.js 22 or later** (with npm) and Git; check with `node --version`. ```sh npx -y @runeditrun/rer dev just-every/run-happytohelp ``` That clones HappyToHelp into `run-happytohelp`, provisions the checkout's own pinned Node and pnpm, installs dependencies, sets up a local owner and starts the app. To set it up without starting it, use `npx -y @runeditrun/rer setup just-every/run-happytohelp`. Without Node, `curl -fsSL https://runeditrun.com/install.sh | sh -s -- dev just-every/run-happytohelp` brings its own. To start it again later, run `cd run-happytohelp && rer dev`. The install also downloads Chromium (about 280 MB, into your user cache) the first time: `rer verify` and the browser checks run in it. Dev uses its local address for the chat widget and generates a private owner password. Wait for `RER_READY`, then open the `RER_OPEN` address to enter as the real local owner and reach **Setup**. No private answers, email service or AI account are needed. Use `rer dev --stop` from the checkout to stop the managed app. Already running 0.3? Keep your checkout and data, and follow [Upgrading from 0.3.x](OPERATIONS.md#upgrading-from-03x) instead. See [Install](docs/INSTALLER.md) for private setup answers and [Local command reference](RUN-LOCALLY.md) for ports, preview and idle shutdown. To try the customer flow, [install the widget on a local page](docs/INSTALLER.md#try-the-customer-widget-locally), send a visitor message and reply from **Inbox**. Set that page's exact origin in **Settings → Widget → Settings**; the app's own origin remains allowed. A visitor's entered email can receive operator replies even when their identity is labelled **Unverified**. Local visitor and teammate mail is suppressed without storage or external sending. With a hosted sender, **Email sent to provider · delivery not confirmed** on a reply means acceptance, not confirmed inbox delivery. ## Choose how to run it Local dev is a loopback trial on your computer. An online installation in your own Cloudflare account lets the widget on your website reach the workspace. Both use the same rer commands. An independently managed project may select its own operating contract; this seed's CLI is not a platform admission requirement. ## Deploy to your own Cloudflare account For a new installation, acquire **`v0.4.25` once published**, after installing `rer` as shown above: ```sh git clone --branch v0.4.25 https://github.com/just-every/run-happytohelp cd run-happytohelp ``` Start with a local build and validation: ```sh rer deploy --dry-run ``` This needs no provider credentials, makes no Cloudflare requests, sends no mail and changes nothing remotely. It validates the deployment declaration and builds the application locally. The completion report lists any inputs needed for a real deploy; remote resources, credential validity, target secrets and remote readiness remain unchecked. For a real deployment, read [deployment prerequisites](OPERATIONS.md#deploy-to-your-cloudflare-account). When rer says **See the deploy-kit owner-account instructions**, it means [What you need first](OPERATIONS.md#what-you-need-first): how to make the Cloudflare API token and find the account ID. Configure the real declaration and private account credentials, then: ```sh rer deploy --environment production ``` The contract also requires a separately started **read-only provider preflight** with explicit owner consent and the owner's scoped Cloudflare token. For an existing Worker, that preflight permits only the account's Workers subdomain and the Worker's settings and secret names (three GETs), with no mail or mutations. That separate preflight is not yet implemented or live-qualified; the local dry run does not perform it or prove remote readiness. For a new installation with outbound email, also supply real `EMAIL_PROVIDER`, `EMAIL_FROM`, `EMAIL_API_KEY` and `OWNER_EMAIL` inputs in an owned 0600 `--env-file`; the owner email must receive sign-in mail. Existing installations retain held secrets. The seven optional mailbox settings can stay unset. Remote provisioning remains separately unqualified. ```sh rer deploy --environment production --env-file ~/happytohelp-production.env ``` Deployment provisions declared resources, applies migrations, publishes and checks health through Base deploy-kit. After a healthy deploy, `rer deploy` claims the owner named by `OWNER_EMAIL` (a real setup owner, or the value you supply privately) with a one-time token it then removes. Open your Worker's address and sign in by email as that owner to reach **Setup**. The owner's name is derived from their email. A Workers hostname does not name your business: a `workers.dev` website defaults to **My workspace** regardless of owner email. An explicitly chosen native workspace name takes precedence; you can change it in Project settings. Deploy refuses the local placeholder `owner@run-happytohelp.test`: it has no mailbox. For a real deployment, supply `OWNER_EMAIL` privately in your environment or an owned 0600 `--env-file`. The local dry run can list missing production inputs without requiring them. `rer signin --environment production` directs you to this installation's `/login` page. HappyToHelp uses its native email/password sign-in; the command cannot mint an owner link. If mail fails, follow the working mail recovery in [operations](OPERATIONS.md#claim-your-new-installation). `rer deploy --environment NAME --remove --yes` removes that environment's created Worker, D1, R2 and queues in one pass, including uploaded attachments in its R2 bucket, and reads back that each is gone. Export anything you need before removal. Hosted installation and real provider execution are not qualified by this release. ## What you need and what it costs HappyToHelp is MIT licensed with no seats or subscription fees. Your Cloudflare, email and optional AI providers bill your own accounts. Enable R2 and the account capabilities required by the declaration before deployment. An email sender must be verified. Local development needs no external mail or AI credential. Configure optional model keys, the Apify crawler (for website sources larger than the built-in reader's 40 pages; see [Website knowledge](docs/website-knowledge.md)), Qdrant search, GitHub and email only when you need them. See [Optional features and their settings](OPERATIONS.md#optional-features-and-their-settings) and [Measure local usage and costs](OPERATIONS.md#measure-local-usage-and-costs). The optional [local agent](local-agent/README.md) runs on the computer doing the support work and has its own runtime prerequisites. ## After you install Your workspace is already set up when you first sign in. It has a starter assistant for visitors, a reply-by-email mailbox when the installation holds an `INBOUND_EMAIL_TOKEN`, and mail that leaves from the installation's own sender until your sending domain is verified. The inbound token authenticates incoming mail; configure your email provider's domain routing and webhook before replies can arrive. Creating the workspace may send you one welcome email. Use **Setup**, the first entry in **Settings** (its row there counts what still needs you; an empty inbox links to it): **Needs you** lists what cannot be done for you (the widget on your website, an AI key and, with a hosted email provider, your sending domain's DNS records), and **What we've set** lists the rest. Anything under **Needs you** can be skipped for now and picked up later from **Skipped**. The system runs its own checks while Setup is open, and what it confirms is counted ("N of M confirmed", without what you skipped): mail to you, sender DNS, inbound mail, model access, spend ceilings, widget origin and an authenticated widget visit. Saved settings alone do not complete them. Add the widget through **Settings → Widget**, set its exact [website origin](docs/SETUP-WORKFLOW.md#the-widget-website-origin), publish useful articles and invite teammates through **Settings → Agents**. By default the widget does not ask for an email. For visitors to receive replies by email, enable **Settings → Widget → Settings → Required contact details → Require email**. The visitor enters their address before sending a message; operator replies can then use it on a hosted installation with email sending configured. ## Set up AI replies Your starter assistant answers visitors by itself, from the help articles you publish and from what we read on your website, and within your daily limits, as soon as the installation has a key from an AI provider. Until then, new conversations stay with your team and the AI page and Setup say a key is missing. 1. **Get an API key** from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, xAI or OpenRouter. The provider bills you for what you use. 2. **Add the key to your installation** under the name for that provider: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY` (or `GEMINI_API_KEY`), `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. The setup answers can store one at install time (see [Install](docs/INSTALLER.md#private-setup-answers)). - **On Cloudflare:** in the Cloudflare dashboard, open your Worker, go to **Settings → Variables and Secrets** and add the key as a secret. You can also set it in your terminal before you run `rer deploy --environment production` (see [Optional features and their settings](OPERATIONS.md#optional-features-and-their-settings)). - **On your own computer:** add a line such as `OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key` to a file named `.dev.vars` in the `run-happytohelp` folder, then restart the app. 3. **Setup notices the key.** While the starter assistant is untouched it uses a model of whichever provider's key is installed, and Setup confirms the key with the provider. To use a different assistant, open **Settings → AI**, add one (or choose **Customize** on an existing one), enter the **Model** it uses and keep it **Enabled**. Then, under **Responder defaults**, choose which assistant answers visitors, and with **AI replies** whether its replies are sent automatically, kept as drafts for your team to send, or turned off. In draft, a reply your local computer agent prepares waits in its report for you to use and send, and a visitor who writes while your team is away gets your away message, as if no assistant were assigned. Such a visitor's conversation also appears in **Open** and **Unassigned**. Keep key values out of chat messages and the browser. To cap what visitors can spend, see [Limits and AI ceilings](docs/PUBLIC-LIMITS.md). ## Try a demo inbox When your workspace has no conversations yet, the inbox greets you with one next action and a quiet **Try a demo inbox** link under it. The link creates a separate, clearly labelled workspace called **Demo inbox · Northstar Outfitters**, with: - fictional customer conversations - a drafting assistant you can edit - three published FAQ articles Creating the demo makes no AI, email or other provider calls. To see AI drafting, open a demo conversation and press **Generate**. HappyToHelp then drafts suggested replies for you to review, using your AI provider. The demo's assistant uses OpenAI's `gpt-5.6-luna` model, so this needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` unless you change the assistant's model (see [Set up AI replies](#set-up-ai-replies)). Generate never sends a reply to a customer. When you are done, delete the demo workspace from its settings. ## Support history, feedback, Reports and connections Owner/admin **Move in** reviews five kinds: conversations, contacts, tags, saved replies and articles. Inspect per-kind plans, rejections, omissions, conflicts and publication changes; approve, resume a stopped batch, follow report links, repeat or undo through the same current role checks. Original source IDs, timestamps and private notes remain attributed; published articles stay published and drafts stay drafts. Apply and undo are inert: no mail, widget messages, model work, assignment or connection notifications. [The moving-in guide](docs/moving-in.md) explains formats, source custody and conflict-safe undo. Validation is **documented-format, synthetic-only; realExport: not-supplied**. The 9 October owner ruling requires exact business-state equality on repeat and undo. Platform counters/sequences, audit and import journals are excluded; business notes, source links, identities and native contact content remain checked. A resolved widget conversation asks **Did this answer your question?** with thumbs up/down and an optional comment up to 1,000 characters. Only its owning visitor session can rate its current closed cycle; widget action limits apply and changes retain history. Native records store AI, assisted, human or unknown provenance. A visitor message reopens the conversation; another resolution gets its own record. Reports uses the workspace timezone and 7/30/90-day or custom calendar ranges for volume, median/p90 first response and resolution times, AI resolution and satisfaction counts/rates, daily series and latest comments with conversation links. Conversation and summary CSV exports guard formula-leading cells. Imports are excluded and Reports calls no model. [The Reports guide](docs/reports.md) and [workspace workflows](docs/WORKSPACE-WORKFLOWS.md) explain the denominators. Settings offers seven explicit token scopes, optional expiry, one-time secret display, hashed storage, revoke, last use and audit. [The API guide](docs/api.md) contains thirteen Bearer-only operations. Webhooks support four signed events, explicit test sends and safe attempt logs; public HTTPS destinations are checked against SSRF. Slack has incoming-webhook and bot-plus-channel modes. Both have recorded-response checks only; **live Slack: not-supplied**. Deliveries use ordinary platform HTTPS fetch with manual redirects. Every 3xx fails without following its Location. Requests are limited to 1 MiB, responses (including streams) to 64 KiB, and the entire request/response to 10 seconds. Public HTTPS destination syntax and literal IP validation remain enforced; this edition does not claim DNS pinning. Base HTTP 500 remains uncertain without automatic replay; 429 retains four bounded attempts with the same logical identity and exact body. Installed owners land on the Setup page, where the system has already done what it can and lists only what needs them; new workspaces lead with the widget snippet, with secrets and verification controls under **Advanced**. Empty inboxes offer widget installation, a link to Setup and a demo. Workspace headers follow the selected workspace; visitors intentionally see the operator's display name. Local development suppresses email without storing messages. ## Export conversations In **Reports**, choose **Export workspace conversations (JSON)**. The `transcripts.json` download includes every workspace conversation across all dates and imports, with its messages, private notes and attachment names and metadata. Attachment bytes remain in the workspace; use the portable backup for those. Exports ask for recent confirmation: accounts without a second factor can choose **Email me a sign-in link**, press **Sign in** from their mailbox in the same browser, then return and press **Continue**. This also works for older email-claimed owners whose generated password was never known. After mailbox confirmation, **Profile → Security** lets you set a new password without the old one. Enrolled second factors remain required. Reports and its analytics CSVs exclude empty widget conversations. ## Contributor setup For work on the source, select Node **22.20.0** and pnpm **10.12.4**: ```sh pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm exec rer describe --json pnpm exec rer check --profile first-party ``` ## Verify ```sh rer verify ``` The complete target checks the contract, real build, typecheck, native runtime, command journey, current workflows and selected Base copies. For a change, run its touched tests plus `pnpm run typecheck`; CI is the full wall. Browser suites and full verification run on the designated remote runner. Provider fixtures prove local protocol behavior; hosted acceptance and paid-provider execution require separate evidence. Preserve [the current holds](HANDOVER.md#acceptance-boundaries). ## Where to go next Development lives in [just-every/run-happytohelp](https://github.com/just-every/run-happytohelp); the private repository is retained for research and evidence only. - [Install](docs/INSTALLER.md): private answers and the rer journey. - [First-run setup](docs/SETUP-WORKFLOW.md): one-screen first run and the Setup page. - [Operations](OPERATIONS.md): configuration, data movement, deployment and recovery. - [Updates and recovery](docs/INDEPENDENT-RELEASE.md): owner customizations and backups. - [Product contract](CONTRACT.md) and [acceptance](ACCEPTANCE.md): requirements and proof. - [Authoring](docs/AUTHORING.md): source selection and exact Base copies. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Third-party asset notices remain under [docs/licenses](docs/licenses).

# Lamp target product contract

This is the product Lamp is being built towards: a full replacement for Atlassian Statuspage, Better Stack Status Pages and Status.io that also goes past Instatus and incident.io Status Pages. A buyer of any of those products should be able to switch to Lamp. The document states the whole target and, clause by clause, how close the current build is.

## Product target

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Category | Status pages and incident communication |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | Atlassian Statuspage, Better Stack Status Pages, Status.io |
| Up-and-comers it must also beat | Instatus, incident.io Status Pages |
| First buyer | A US software or SaaS business, priced in USD, that runs a public status page and tells its customers what is happening during an incident, and is moving off Atlassian Statuspage, Better Stack Status Pages or Status.io |

The primary journey: An operator sets up the page and components, accepts evidence, drafts and publishes an impact-first incident update, notifies the subscribers who follow it, keeps the next-update promise, verifies recovery and preserves the report and history.

## How to read this contract

- This follows the RER contract standard.
- Core, Agent surface and Later are measured separately.
- Done means every acceptance point has recorded proof through the product’s doors.
- Real-world-only proof is dated in the non-blocking Field proof register.
- ACCEPTANCE.md and docs/CLAIMS.md are generated from this file.

## Door rules

- **D-1.** A subscriber receives at most one notification per published update per channel, whatever the number of times publication is retried or the queue redelivers its job.
- **D-2.** Webhook subscribers retain their chosen notification format. Notifications preserve the published fields, follow the documented authentication profile and disclose no subscriber address.
